名称.日文: 真岡鐵道モオカ63形気動車

日文.词条标题: 真岡鐵道モオカ63形気動車
日文.首段: 真岡鐵道モオカ63形気動車（もおかてつどうモオカ63がたきどうしゃ）は、真岡鐵道に1988年（昭和63年）から2006年（平成18年）まで在籍していた気動車。

章节.概要:
真岡線が1988年4月1日に第三セクターの真岡鐵道に転換されるのを前に、富士重工業によりモオカ63-1 - モオカ63-8の8両が製造された。当時富士重工業が第3セクター鉄道向けに製造していたLE-CarIIシリーズの一形式である。
開業半年後の1988年10月にモオカ63-9・モオカ63-10を、1993年（平成5年）にモオカ63-11を増備し、計11両となった。
形式の「モオカ」は真岡に、「63」は製造初年の和暦の昭和63年にそれぞれ由来する。ワンマン運転に対応した構造である。
章节.車体:
1985年以降明知鉄道や樽見鉄道・天竜浜名湖鉄道などで採用例のある LE-CarII の15m級普通鋼製車体で、バス車体工法を取り入れており、側面の屋根が浅く、側板にはリベットが打ち込まれている。両端にバス用の折り扉を設置し、乗務員室側にのみ乗務員室扉を設置した。扉間の窓は中間3組だけが上段固定下段横引き窓であり、それ以外の側面窓は固定窓となっている。最終増備車の11は中間5組の窓が上段固定下段横引き窓で、出入口扉の隣の窓のみ固定窓である。
塗装はクリーム色地にスカイブルー・薄緑色・緑色の模様を入れた塗装で、車体裾部分はオレンジ色となっている。
章节.車内:
座席は出入口寄りをロングシート、中間部を向かい合わせの固定クロスシート（ボックスシート）としたセミクロスシートとなっている。トイレは設けられていない。なお1 - 5は1991年（平成3年）2月に全席ロングシートに改造された。
ワンマン運転に対応するため運転室付近に運賃箱・整理券発行機を設置している。運賃表示器は設置せず、三角表を掲示している。
機関直結方式、冷房能力22000kcal/hの冷房装置を装備した。
章节.台車・機器:
エンジンはLE-CarII標準のUDトラックス（旧・日産ディーゼル）PE6Hではなく、地場産業育成の観点から地元栃木県の小松製作所小山工場製のS6D125-H-1（出力250PS/1900rpm）を採用した。これはブルドーザー用エンジンを横型に設計変更し、鉄道車両用としたエンジンである。後に小松は本形式へのエンジン搭載を契機に鉄道車両用エンジンへ参入することになる。JR各社などで導入されているSA6D125Hとは、インタークーラーを備えていない点が異なる。
台車は空気ばね式二軸ボギー台車で、一方が駆動台車、もう一方が付随台車となっている。
章节.廃車: 製造後10年以上が経過し老朽化が進んだため、2002年（平成14年）から2006年（平成18年）にかけてモオカ14形へ置き換えられ、廃車となった。最後まで残ったモオカ63-1・モオカ63-11は2006年（平成18年）12月9日、真岡→茂木→真岡→下館→真岡のルートでさよなら運転を行った。その後しばらく真岡駅に留置されていたが、ミャンマーの鉄道へ譲渡のため、2007年3月19日に陸送にて搬出された。
章节.参考文献: 交友社『鉄道ファン』1988年10月号（通巻330号）特集：第3セクター鉄道のDC

中文.词条标题: 真冈铁道MoOka 63型柴油动车组
中文.首段: 真冈铁道MoOka 63型柴油动车组（もおかてつどうモオカ63がたきどうしゃ）是1988年（昭和63年）至2006年（平成18年）期间配属真冈铁道的柴油动车组。

章节.概要:
在真冈线于1988年4月1日转为第三部门铁道真冈铁道之前，由富士重工业制造了MoOka 63-1至MoOka 63-8共8辆。这是当时富士重工业为第三部门铁道制造的LE-CarII系列中的一个形式。
开业半年后的1988年10月增备了MoOka 63-9、MoOka 63-10，1993年（平成5年）又增备了MoOka 63-11，共计11辆。
形式名中的“モオカ”取自真冈，“63”则取自制造首年的和历昭和63年。本型车采用适应单人运转的结构。
章节.车体:
采用1985年以后明知铁道、樽见铁道、天龙滨名湖铁道等已有采用先例的LE-CarII的15米级普通钢制车体，引入了客车（巴士）车体工艺，侧面的车顶较浅，侧板上打有铆钉。两端设置客车用折叠门，仅在乘务员室一侧设置乘务员室门。车门之间的窗仅中间3组为上部固定、下部横拉式窗，其余的侧面窗均为固定窗。最后增备的11号车中间5组窗为上部固定、下部横拉式窗，仅出入口门旁的窗为固定窗。
涂装为奶油色底配天蓝色、浅绿色、绿色的花纹，车体裙部为橙色。
章节.车内:
座椅为出入口附近设纵向长条座椅、中间部设面对面固定横排座椅（箱式座椅）的半交叉式座椅。未设置厕所。另外1至5号车于1991年（平成3年）2月改造为全席纵向长条座椅。
为适应单人运转，在驾驶室附近设置了投币箱、整理券发行机。未设置票价显示牌，而是张贴三角表。
装备了发动机直结方式、制冷能力22000kcal/h的空调装置。
章节.台车・机器:
发动机未采用LE-CarII标准的UD Trucks（原日产柴油机）PE6H，而是出于培育地方产业的考虑，采用了本地栃木县小松制作所小山工厂制造的S6D125-H-1（输出250PS/1900rpm）。这是将推土机用发动机改为卧式设计、转用于铁路车辆的发动机。后来小松正是以本型车搭载发动机为契机进入铁路车辆用发动机领域。它与JR各公司等引进的SA6D125H的不同之处在于未配备中间冷却器。
转向架为空气弹簧式二轴转向架，其中一个为驱动转向架，另一个为从动转向架。
章节.廃車: 由于制造后经过10年以上、老化加剧，2002年（平成14年）至2006年（平成18年）期间被MoOka 14型替换而报废。最后保留的MoOka 63-1、MoOka 63-11于2006年（平成18年）12月9日，沿真冈→茂木→真冈→下馆→真冈的路线进行了告别运转。此后一段时间停放在真冈站，后为转让给缅甸的铁路，于2007年3月19日通过陆路运输运出。
章节.参考文献: 交友社《铁道Fan》1988年10月号（总第330号）特集：第三部门铁道的DC

英文.词条标题: Mooka Railway MoOka 63 series diesel railcar
英文.首段: The Mooka Railway MoOka 63 series diesel railcar (Mooka Tetsudō Mooka 63-gata kidōsha) was a diesel railcar that belonged to Mooka Railway from 1988 (Shōwa 63) to 2006 (Heisei 18).

章节.Overview:
Before the Mooka Line was converted on April 1, 1988 to the third-sector Mooka Railway, Fuji Heavy Industries built eight cars, MoOka 63-1 to MoOka 63-8. It was one of the LE-CarII series that Fuji Heavy Industries was building for third-sector railways at the time.
Half a year after opening, in October 1988 MoOka 63-9 and MoOka 63-10 were added, and in 1993 (Heisei 5) MoOka 63-11 was added, for a total of 11 cars.
The "Mooka" in the type name derives from Mooka, and "63" from Shōwa 63, the Japanese era year of first manufacture. It was designed for one-man operation.
章节.Car body:
It used the 15 m-class ordinary steel body of the LE-CarII, which had been adopted since 1985 by the Akichi Railway, Tarumi Railway, Tenryū Hamanako Railway and others; it incorporated bus body construction, with a shallow roof profile on the sides and rivets driven into the side panels. Bus-type folding doors were fitted at both ends, and a crew door was provided only on the crew compartment side. Of the windows between the doors, only the middle three groups were of the fixed-upper, horizontally-sliding-lower type, while the other side windows were fixed. On the last car added, No. 11, the middle five groups of windows were of the fixed-upper, horizontally-sliding-lower type, with only the window next to the entrance door being fixed.
The livery was a cream base with a pattern of sky blue, light green and green, with the body skirt in orange.
章节.Interior:
The seating was semi-cross seating, with longitudinal bench seats near the entrances and facing fixed cross seats (box seats) in the middle. No toilet was provided. Cars 1-5 were converted to all-longitudinal seating in February 1991 (Heisei 3).
To support one-man operation, a fare box and a numbered-ticket issuing machine were installed near the driver's cab. No fare display was installed; instead a triangular fare table was posted.
An engine-direct air-conditioning unit with a cooling capacity of 22,000 kcal/h was fitted.
章节.Bogies and equipment:
For the engine, instead of the LE-CarII-standard UD Trucks (formerly Nissan Diesel) PE6H, the S6D125-H-1 (output 250 PS/1900 rpm) made by the Komatsu Oyama plant in local Tochigi Prefecture was adopted from the standpoint of fostering local industry. This was a bulldozer engine redesigned as a horizontal type for railway use. Later, Komatsu would enter the railway-vehicle engine field, with its installation in this type as the trigger. It differs from the SA6D125H adopted by the JR companies and others in that it does not have an intercooler.
The bogies were air-spring two-axle bogies, one being a driving bogie and the other a trailing bogie.
章节.Withdrawal: Because more than ten years had passed since manufacture and aging had progressed, the cars were replaced by the MoOka 14 series and withdrawn between 2002 (Heisei 14) and 2006 (Heisei 18). The last surviving cars, MoOka 63-1 and MoOka 63-11, made a farewell run on December 9, 2006 (Heisei 18) over the route Mooka → Motegi → Mooka → Shimodate → Mooka. They were kept at Mooka Station for a while afterward, but were transported out by road on March 19, 2007 for transfer to the railways of Myanmar.
章节.References: Kōyūsha, "Tetsudō Fan," October 1988 issue (No. 330), special feature: DCs of third-sector railways.

The Mooka Railway MoOka 63 series diesel railcar (Mooka Tetsudō Mooka 63-gata kidōsha) was a diesel railcar that belonged to Mooka Railway from 1988 (Shōwa 63) to 2006 (Heisei 18).

== Overview ==
Before the Mooka Line was converted on April 1, 1988 to the third-sector Mooka Railway, Fuji Heavy Industries built eight cars, MoOka 63-1 to MoOka 63-8. It was one of the LE-CarII series that Fuji Heavy Industries was building for third-sector railways at the time.
Half a year after opening, in October 1988 MoOka 63-9 and MoOka 63-10 were added, and in 1993 (Heisei 5) MoOka 63-11 was added, for a total of 11 cars.
The "Mooka" in the type name derives from Mooka, and "63" from Shōwa 63, the Japanese era year of first manufacture. It was designed for one-man operation.

== Structure ==

=== Car body ===
It used the 15 m-class ordinary steel body of the LE-CarII, which had been adopted since 1985 by the Akichi Railway, Tarumi Railway, Tenryū Hamanako Railway and others; it incorporated bus body construction, with a shallow roof profile on the sides and rivets driven into the side panels. Bus-type folding doors were fitted at both ends, and a crew door was provided only on the crew compartment side. Of the windows between the doors, only the middle three groups were of the fixed-upper, horizontally-sliding-lower type, while the other side windows were fixed. On the last car added, No. 11, the middle five groups of windows were of the fixed-upper, horizontally-sliding-lower type, with only the window next to the entrance door being fixed.
The livery was a cream base with a pattern of sky blue, light green and green, with the body skirt in orange.

=== Interior ===
The seating was semi-cross seating, with longitudinal bench seats near the entrances and facing fixed cross seats (box seats) in the middle. No toilet was provided. Cars 1-5 were converted to all-longitudinal seating in February 1991 (Heisei 3).
To support one-man operation, a fare box and a numbered-ticket issuing machine were installed near the driver's cab. No fare display was installed; instead a triangular fare table was posted.
An engine-direct air-conditioning unit with a cooling capacity of 22,000 kcal/h was fitted.

It differs from the SA6D125H adopted by the JR companies and others in that it does not have an intercooler.
The bogies were air-spring two-axle bogies, one being a driving bogie and the other a trailing bogie.

Because more than ten years had passed since manufacture and aging had progressed, the cars were replaced by the MoOka 14 series and withdrawn between 2002 (Heisei 14) and 2006 (Heisei 18). The last surviving cars, MoOka 63-1 and MoOka 63-11, made a farewell run on December 9, 2006 (Heisei 18) over the route Mooka → Motegi → Mooka → Shimodate → Mooka. They were kept at Mooka Station for a while afterward, but were transported out by road on March 19, 2007 for transfer to the railways of Myanmar.
